verdict.rationale: Cooley's own Cooley GO Delaware Incorporation Package Generator documents generating a Certificate of Incorporation, Bylaws and a founder Restricted Stock Purchase Agreement (with IP assignment, plus 83(b) materials when stock vests). Its emerging-companies practice claims 7,000+ high-growth private company clients, and a community post corroborates Cooley GO as a startup forms resource. However, the evidence shows a self-serve generator rather than a documented engagement in which the firm itself handles incorporation, and initial board consents are not shown in the incorporation package. Missing for 10: initial board consents in the incorporation package, explicit documentation of engaging the firm's lawyers for incorporation as a core emerging-companies service, hands-on corroboration of a firm-handled incorporation.

support.subject: As a founder, I can engage the firm to incorporate my company — charter, bylaws, initial board consents, and founder stock purchase — documented as a core of its startup/emerging-companies practice

citations.quote: The Cooley GO Docs Incorporation Package Generator allows you to generate any or all of the following documents: ... Certificate of Incorporation; Bylaws ... Restricted Stock Purchase Agreement, which automatically includes an Assignment Agreement for intellectual property
If the stock is subject to vesting, the following will be included: Form of Section 83(b) Election; Joint Escrow Instructions; Stock Assignment Separate From Certificate
Represent 7,000+ innovative, high-growth private company clients, including 30% of US-based unicorns
Cooley Go is a great resource for legal agreements and forms commonly required by start ups (particularly venture backed startups).
